true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new overload replaces the existing four-dimension downsize API

Ruby does not overload methods by arity. Defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` here replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition, rather than adding a second accepted signature. Any existing caller using the formerly supported width/height form will now raise `ArgumentError` (five arguments supplied to a method accepting three or four), breaking thumbnail/image-processing callers outside this diff.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side validation now ignores both configured image and attachment limits

Replacing `max_<type>_size_kb` with a hard-coded 10 MiB limit means attachments are now accepted by the browser even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller, only to fail on the server later. It also prevents clients from uploading images above 10 MiB when an administrator has configured a larger image limit. The larger pre-processing allowance should be limited to images that can actually be downsized; attachments must continue to use their configured limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Five fixed 80% reductions cannot ensure the upload meets the configured maximum

The reduction loop is capped at five iterations and each iteration only reduces dimensions to 80%, so a 10 MiB image is still roughly 3.3 MiB after all five attempts (and may compress even less effectively depending on image contents). Sites configured with a lower `max_image_size_kb` will still have the upload rejected by `Upload.create_for`, despite this path claiming to automatically reduce images to the allowed size. The resize ratio/iteration strategy needs to be based on the configured target or continue until the target is reached with a safe termination condition.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Updates and deletes of nonexistent hosts raise 500 errors

`update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and immediately call `save_host` or `destroy` without checking whether a row was found. A stale admin page or request for an unknown ID therefore raises `NoMethodError` instead of returning a normal 404/not-found response. Use `find`/`find_by!` or explicitly render a not-found error before dereferencing the record.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy hosts are copied without normalization and stop matching requests

The old setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/path` (the existing tests explicitly cover those forms), but this migration inserts those strings verbatim. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` subsequently extracts only the request hostname and compares it to the stored `host`, so a migrated row containing a scheme or path can never authorize that host. Existing embedding installations using those supported legacy formats will begin rejecting embeds and topic retrievals after migration. Normalize each legacy value to its hostname before inserting it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when the legacy embed_category setting was never persisted

The migration unconditionally indexes the first row returned by the `embed_category` query (`...[0]['id']`). Site settings with their default value are not necessarily stored in `site_settings`, so a deployment that configured allowed hosts but left the category at its default has no `embed_category` row. In that common case `[0]` is nil and the migration aborts before it can fall back to Uncategorized. Handle an empty result before indexing it (and likewise make the fallback query robust).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Duplicate host mappings make the destination category nondeterministic

There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index on `host`, while the admin UI/API permits creating multiple rows for the same host. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record's category, so duplicate entries for one hostname can route imported posts to an arbitrary category depending on database query order. Enforce a case-insensitive unique host constraint (and clean/deduplicate migration input) so each hostname has one unambiguous mapping.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Manual unsubscribe URLs fail with a nil TopicUser record

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when a logged-in user visits an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have not previously viewed or otherwise received a topic-user row for. The following access to `tu.notification_level` then raises a 500 error. The route is publicly reachable and the new client route makes such navigation possible, so the action must create/update the association via `TopicUser.change` or handle a missing record before reading it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
A GET request changes a user's notification preference

`unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` in response to a GET request, and the action is explicitly exempted from the XHR check. Any site can cause a logged-in user's browser to request a known public topic unsubscribe URL (for example with an image or redirect), changing that user's per-topic notification state without consent. State changes should require a CSRF-protected non-GET request, with the email link leading to a confirmation page or a signed one-time action token.

Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change and can be undone by auto-tracking

The action writes `notification_level` directly and leaves `notifications_reason_id` nil for topic-user records created by ordinary visits. `TopicUser.update_last_read` treats a nil reason as eligible for automatic promotion to `tracking`; therefore, after this endpoint mutes such a topic, a later read that crosses the auto-track threshold can silently change it back to tracking and resume topic email notifications. Use the notification-state update path (or explicitly persist a user-changed reason and timestamp) rather than directly saving the record. The direct save also omits the MessageBus notification used to synchronize other open clients.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Match-count updates lose increments under concurrent validation

The counter is updated with a read-modify-write sequence (`record.match_count += 1` followed by `save`). Two concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked address can both read the same count and save the same incremented value, causing one or more matches to be lost. Since this table explicitly records match statistics, use an atomic database update such as `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or locking/counter updates so concurrent attempts are counted correctly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-address matching is case-sensitive and can be trivially bypassed

`should_block?` compares the submitted value directly against the stored string. The signup path assigns `params[:email]` directly to `User#email`, so a row for `bad@spamclub.com` does not match a signup using `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` (or other casing variants) on a case-sensitive database. This differs from the domain restrictions, which use a case-insensitive regexp, and allows a blocked address to register simply by changing case. Normalize both blocked-email records and values being checked with the application's canonical email normalization (for example `Email.downcase(...).strip`), and ensure lookup/indexing uses that normalized form.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Controller success spec expects a synchronous retriever that the controller never invokes

This example sets an expectation on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve`, but `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` instead of constructing a `TopicRetriever`. The expectation is therefore unsatisfied and the added controller spec fails whenever it runs. Update the test to assert the `Jobs.enqueue` call (and cover execution in the retrieve-job spec), or change the implementation if synchronous retrieval was intended.

Direct article retrieval does not load open-uri before calling open

`import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file does not require `open-uri`. The only new `require 'open-uri'` is in `Jobs::PollFeed`, which is not loaded on the normal embed retrieval path when feed polling is disabled. In a normal process where nothing else happened to load it, Kernel#open treats the HTTP URL as a file path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so requested embeds can never be imported. Require `open-uri` in this dependency's own file (or use an explicit HTTP client).

Imported feed HTML is stored and served without sanitization

`import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns that raw HTML unchanged. Feed items are passed directly to this method by `PollFeed`, so a `<script>`, event handler, iframe, or other active markup in an RSS/Atom item is persisted and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed and normal topic views. A compromised feed or untrusted content included by a feed can therefore execute JavaScript under the Discourse origin, including in an administrator's session. Sanitize imported HTML with the normal allowlist/cooking pipeline (or a strict dedicated sanitizer) before storing it, rather than bypassing cooking.

Remote retrieval follows redirects without validating the final destination

The host check in `TopicRetriever` only validates the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects. An allowed embed host with an open redirect (or a compromised allowed host) can redirect the worker to localhost, cloud metadata addresses, or other internal services; their response is then imported into a public topic. Validate every redirect target against an allowlist and block private/reserved IP ranges, or disable redirects and fetch only the validated origin.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Flex layout disables the action button's right float

`.small-action` is now a flex container, so its direct `button` child is a flex item. Per the flexbox layout rules, the existing `float: right` on that item computes to `none`; without `margin-left: auto`, `justify-content`, or another positioning rule, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge. This regresses the placement of small-action controls and can push them off the row when the description is wide. Add an explicit flex alignment rule (for example `margin-left: auto` on the button, with appropriate shrinking/growth for the description).

The flex alignment mixin omits the Mozilla legacy box property

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` deliberately emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box`, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. Firefox versions using the legacy box implementation will therefore ignore every `@include align-items(...)` call and use the legacy default alignment (stretch), including the newly centered header contents and baseline-aligned bullet badges. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside the other legacy declarations, or remove the unsupported legacy display mode if that browser family is no longer supported.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The website_name inclusion predicate is not named according to serializer convention

Serializer conditional methods in this class use the `include_<attribute>?` form (for example, `include_email?` and `include_card_image_badge?`). This method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so the serializer will not invoke it as the condition for `:website_name`; profiles without a website can therefore receive a `website_name: null` field instead of omitting it as intended. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and apply the same visibility condition as `website`.

false_positives.candidate:
Sibling hostnames are treated as the same domain using an unsafe label-count heuristic

For any two hostnames with more than two labels, this compares everything except the first label. That incorrectly treats unrelated registrable domains under multi-part public suffixes as the same domain: with an instance at `forum.github.io`, a website at `alice.github.io/private` will display `alice.github.io/private`, despite being a different site; the same occurs for hosts under `co.uk` and other public suffixes. The decision to expose the full path should use a public-suffix-aware registrable-domain comparison (or restrict it to exact hostname/known instance-domain relationships), rather than dropping the first DNS label.

website_name bypasses the existing anonymous TL0 privacy restriction

`website` is explicitly listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so an anonymous viewer of a TL0 profile does not receive it. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not subject to that restriction, but is derived directly from the hidden website and can include both its host and path. As a result, anonymous clients receive profile URL information that the serializer intentionally withholds (for example, `example.com/private-profile`) even though `website` itself is absent. Add `website_name` to the same conditional visibility policy as `website` (and ensure its include predicate follows that policy).

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact multiples of the page size produce an extra empty page

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is one too high whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. For example, a group with 50 members and a limit of 50 displays two pages; clicking Next requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use a ceiling division (for example `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`) while retaining the explicit zero-member case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Out-of-order membership requests can replace the currently selected page

Every `findMembers` completion unconditionally writes `offset`, `members`, and pagination metadata to the shared group model. A user can click Next and then Previous before the first request returns; if the Previous request completes first and the older Next request completes afterward, the stale Next response overwrites the first-page result and changes the displayed page back to the stale offset. Track/request-cancel the latest fetch (or verify the response offset/request token before applying it) so only the current request updates the model.

The existing members endpoint response contract is changed incompatibly

`GET /groups/:group_id/members` previously returned a serialized JSON array of users, but now returns an object containing `members` and `meta`. The in-repository Ember consumer was updated, but any other client, plugin, or API integration using this established endpoint will now fail when it attempts to iterate the top-level response. Preserve the array contract or introduce/version a metadata-aware endpoint before changing this response shape.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback translations are only loaded for controller requests

The lazy translation loader only loads the current locale during `I18n.translate`; a fallback lookup performed by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` reads the fallback locale directly from the backend and does not invoke `I18n.translate` again. This callback preloads fallback locales only for requests that pass through `ApplicationController`. Mailers, background jobs, model/service code, and any other `I18n.t` call outside that controller will therefore load (for example) `fr` but not the configured site locale or `en`, so missing French strings still resolve as missing translations on a cold process. Fallback locale loading needs to happen as part of translation/fallback resolution rather than only in this controller filter.

Translation cache does not include the dynamic fallback chain

A no-options translation is cached only by key, current locale, and backend object. The new fallback result also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which can be changed at runtime, but this change adds no cache invalidation for that setting. After changing the site default locale, keys absent from a user's locale can continue returning the old default locale's cached text until the entry is evicted or I18n is reloaded, producing stale and inconsistent server-rendered translations.

Neither `UsernameForm` nor `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` supplies a no-argument overload. This source therefore does not compile; pass `context.getUser()` or add the intended overload.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an anonymous initial login

The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` predicate requires a non-null user. true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing

The new advanced path intentionally passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django `QuerySet` does not support negative indexing or slicing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` A client can supply a cursor with a negative offset, so an authorized user opting into this paginator can turn such a request into a 500 rather than receiving a valid page or a pagination validation error. Clamp or explicitly reject negative offsets; negative offsets cannot implement reverse traversal through ORM slicing.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs

`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime` from each `AuditLogEntry`. This implementation calls `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`, which raises `TypeError` for datetimes when `build_cursor` constructs the response cursors. Consequently every authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` that returns audit-log rows will fail with a 500. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible timestamp conversion (or should subclass/reuse `DateTimePaginator`) rather than numeric rounding.

Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs

`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering `AuditLogEntry` by `-datetime`. This paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the field value, which is a `datetime`, so building cursors for any non-empty optimized response raises `TypeError`. Even if that were avoided, `value_from_cursor` returns a numeric cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime for the subsequent queryset filter. Thus an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 on a non-empty audit-log response. This endpoint needs a datetime-aware paginator (or the optimized paginator needs the DateTimePaginator key/cursor conversion behavior).

false_negatives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Changing Redis collection type breaks existing buffered segments during rollout

This writes each existing `span-buf:s:*` key with `ZADD`, whereas previously the same keys were Redis sets populated with `SADD`. Buffered keys can remain for up to `redis_ttl` (default one hour), so a rolling deployment will encounter old set keys: `ZADD` will return WRONGTYPE, and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` and new flusher's `ZSCAN` likewise cannot operate on them. This can repeatedly fail consumer batches and prevent both ingestion and flushing until the old keys expire. Use versioned keys or provide a compatibility/migration path before switching the Redis data structure.

Eviction ignores the configured max_segment_spans limit

The buffer still exposes `max_segment_spans` as a constructor option, but the only span-count enforcement is now hard-coded to 1000 in Lua. The previous flush-side limit used `self.max_segment_spans`; after this change custom deployments cannot lower or raise the limit, and segments between their configured limit and 1000 are emitted rather than rejected/limited as configured. Pass the configured limit to the script and enforce that value, or remove/document the option and update callers if a fixed 1000-span contract is intentional.

Redirect traversal limit is reduced and can split deep traces

The redirect-chain traversal limit is reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose buffered parent chain exceeds 1,000 links, the script stops resolving redirects and attaches the arriving span to an intermediate buffer rather than the root buffer. Those buffers can then be queued and flushed as separate segments, producing incorrect segment IDs and incomplete trace segments. Retain the prior limit or add a safe chain-compression strategy rather than silently reducing the supported tree depth.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but eligibility is evaluated against the `dataset` captured from the original request. In the dashboard split path, an enhanced-metrics widget can call `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query, ...)` while the captured dataset is a metrics dataset. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` rejects metrics datasets, so this explicitly error-only Discover subquery is never upsampled despite all projects being allowlisted. Evaluate eligibility against `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` argument rather than the original request context.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw substring check enables upsampling for non-error Discover queries

The Discover eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. This is not a semantic query check: for example, `!event.type:error` (a supported syntax used elsewhere in this endpoint) contains that substring but explicitly selects non-error events, and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` selects transactions as well. Those queries will be rewritten to sum `sample_weight`, even though transactions/non-error events do not have error sampling weights, producing failed queries or incorrect counts. Determine event-type constraints from the parsed query and require that the query cannot include non-error event types.

The internal upsampling aggregate is exposed to client queries

`upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the adjacent internal aggregate. As a result, clients can request `upsampled_count()` directly through Discover/Event Stats without passing the allowlist and event-type checks in `error_upsampling.py`. This permits unallowlisted or mixed-event queries to use `sample_weight`, yielding unsupported/incorrect results (or query failures where the field is unavailable). Mark the function private and expose it only through the guarded rewrite.

Upsampled counts truncate fractional sampling weights

The implementation applies `toInt64` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Sampling rates are floats (the added test factory explicitly converts `client_sample_rate` to float), so weights such as `1 / 0.3` and sums of heterogeneous weights are not necessarily integral. Casting the final sum to an integer truncates the estimate and systematically underreports error counts. Return the numeric sum directly, or use the established rounding behavior for sampled-count estimates if the API contract requires integral counts.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-gated dashboard tables discard the query result

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` instead of the current `result.data`, `result.meta`, and widget field configuration. Consequently every table widget for enabled organizations renders an empty table with no headers or rows, even though the query completed successfully. Pass the actual table result and derived columns/renderers into the new visualization before enabling this path.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Browser report age accepts invalid negative values and zero-valued mixed fields

`age` has no non-negative constraint even though the Reporting API age is an elapsed duration, so reports with a negative age are accepted. In addition, the mutual-exclusion checks at lines 52 and 58 use truthiness; a report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes validation even though the endpoint intends these alternative-format fields to be mutually exclusive. Validate field presence rather than truthiness and set `min_value=0` for `age`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization

The React Query key contains only the date/project/type query options and omits `organization.slug`, whereas the request made by `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` is organization-scoped. In particular, an all-project query has no project IDs and will readily collide when navigating between organizations with the same time range. The hook also deliberately returns the previous data while a fetch is in progress, so keys from the prior organization can be displayed in the next organization's Explore UI. Include the organization slug (or endpoint path) in `queryKey` to prevent cross-organization cache reuse.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup codes are not consumed atomically

The code is looked up from an earlier user read and then consumed with an unconditional update. Two concurrent credential callbacks using the same backup code can both find the code before either update commits, and both will successfully authenticate; each writes the same remaining-code list afterward. This violates the advertised exactly-once property and can issue multiple sessions from one recovery code. Consume the code in a transaction/conditional update tied to the previously read encrypted value (or store codes in individually deletable rows) and reject the request if the conditional update affects no row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code authentication can bypass the account password

The password verification at lines 121-129 is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty, while the new backup-code branch takes precedence whenever `backupCode` is supplied. A caller can therefore submit a valid backup code plus any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` and authenticate without providing the user's password. Backup codes are intended to replace the authenticator factor, not the primary password; this turns a stolen backup code into a standalone login credential. Require password verification whenever this is a CAL password login, independent of which second-factor field is used.

Existing 2FA users have no way to obtain backup codes

The migration adds `backupCodes` as NULL for every existing user, but this endpoint rejects every user who already has 2FA enabled with `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`. Consequently, pre-existing 2FA users receive `MissingBackupCodes` if they choose Lost access and cannot follow the UI instruction to generate codes in settings without first disabling and re-enabling 2FA (which itself requires the unavailable authenticator). Provide a secure backup-code generation/recovery action for already-enabled users, or avoid offering the recovery path until codes have been provisioned.

Users in the external TOTP login flow cannot use backup codes

When `totpEmail` is present (the signed redirect used after Google/SAML 2FA), the page renders `ExternalTotpFooter` rather than `TwoFactorFooter`. That footer only has Cancel, so it does not expose the new Lost access action and there is no way to render or submit `BackupCode` for these users. This leaves accounts that already use the external-provider 2FA flow unable to use the advertised recovery mechanism; expose the backup-code switch in this flow as well and ensure the credentials authorization path accepts it.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar

`destinationCalendar` is optional and is now commonly represented as an empty array. Destructuring an empty array makes `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, but this condition immediately reads `.integration`. Any booking with Google Meet selected but no destination calendar will throw before the calendar/video event is created, rather than falling back to Daily as intended. Guard this access with optional chaining or treat a missing destination calendar as non-Google.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug is no longer stored when team billing is disabled

The previous condition stored `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false. This change reverses that behavior and omits the slug entirely in that mode. Since organization URLs and collision checks use the slug, organizations created with team billing disabled can no longer be addressed by their requested subdomain/slug. This unrelated condition change should be reverted unless the corresponding organization routing/storage behavior was migrated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
CalDAV collective events only target the first destination calendar

For each destination credential, EventManager calls this calendar service, but event creation filters the calendars returned for that credential using only `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. Consequently, later collective hosts either have no matching calendar (so no event is created) or target the first host's URL, which is not accessible with their credentials. The target must be resolved per credential/destination rather than globally from index zero.

Confirming a collective booking loses all non-primary host destinations

This handler reconstructs the event from the booking using only its single `destinationCalendar` relation (or the confirming user's calendar) and wraps that one item in an array. It does not load the collective event type's hosts or their destination calendars. Thus a pending/confirmation-required collective booking will create calendar references only for the primary host when confirmed, even though normal booking creation now includes all hosts. Persist/load the full destination set or rebuild it from the collective hosts before calling `handleConfirmation`.

Lark collective events are written to the first host calendar for every credential

The collective-event loop creates an event for each destination/credential, but Lark derives `calendarId` solely from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`. A Lark credential belonging to a subsequent host will try to write to the first host's calendar and will fail authorization or place the event incorrectly. Select the destination calendar associated with the active credential instead of destructuring the first element.

Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each occurrence

Inside the loop over all calendar references, the recurring branch finds a single reference with `updBooking.references.find(...)`. For a collective booking each occurrence has multiple calendar references, so only the first one is selected; the code then retries that same reference through every calendar credential and never deletes the other hosts' events. This leaves orphaned events in non-primary host calendars (and can issue deletion requests with the wrong credential). Iterate every calendar reference and use its recorded credential ID when deleting it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The minimum sync response schema strips every expiry field

The computed property names here are evaluated to the literal string `"[object Object]"`; they do not create dynamic Zod properties. The second duplicate property also overwrites the first, and `z.object()` strips all unrecognized fields by default. Consequently, when credential syncing is enabled, a normal sync response such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` is parsed down to only `access_token` (plus the synthetic refresh token). Callers such as the Zoom adapter then calculate an expiry using `newTokens.expires_in`, which is undefined, producing `NaN` and potentially failing the credential update; other adapters retain stale expiry values and repeatedly refresh.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh stores the Zod safe-parse wrapper as the credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this update stores that result itself as `credential.key` rather than `key.data`. This occurs for every Google token refresh, including when sync is disabled. On the next use, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives the wrapper instead of Google credentials and rejects it, leaving the user with an unusable Google Calendar connection.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
HubSpot treats a fetch Response from the sync endpoint as a HubSpot token

The native HubSpot refresh API returns a token object directly, but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` whenever syncing is enabled. This code casts that Response to `HubspotToken` and immediately reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken`; both are undefined because the response body is never parsed. It then persists the Response-shaped object and sets the HubSpot client access token to undefined, so synced HubSpot credentials cannot refresh or create meetings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal user ID to the sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the owning Cal user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId` instead. The external app store will therefore look up a user whose ID equals the database credential ID, usually returning no credential and, in the event of an ID collision, potentially returning another user's token.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
HubSpot treats a fetch Response from the sync endpoint as a HubSpot token

The native HubSpot refresh API returns a token object directly, but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` whenever syncing is enabled. This code casts that Response to `HubspotToken` and immediately reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken`; both are undefined because the response body is never parsed. It then persists the Response-shaped object and sets the HubSpot client access token to undefined, so synced HubSpot credentials cannot refresh or create meetings.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it

This file now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but its imports do not include `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. TypeScript compilation of the app-store package will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, preventing this change from building.

Webhook credential create/update is not atomic

The handler performs `findFirst` followed by either `update` or `create`, with no transaction or uniqueness constraint. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create duplicates. Later deliveries update an arbitrary `findFirst` result while stale duplicate credentials remain eligible for use, so the app store can no longer reliably be the source of truth.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest addresses are neither normalized nor deduplicated on the server

The API schema permits duplicate email addresses and this filter only excludes addresses already present on the booking; it does not deduplicate `guests` itself and compares addresses case-sensitively. A direct API caller can submit the same address repeatedly (or an existing/blacklisted address with different casing). Depending on the attendee database constraint this either creates duplicate attendees or makes the whole mutation fail, and casing can bypass the blacklist or create a second representation of the same mailbox. Normalize addresses and deduplicate them server-side before checking existing attendees, the blacklist, and `createMany`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team administrators and owners are incorrectly denied access

The authorization check requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner (`isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`). Those roles are distinct, so a team admin or owner who is not the booking organizer/attendee will be rejected even though the UI and variable name indicate either role should be permitted. Use an OR check (or the existing team-admin-or-owner authorization helper) so either authorized role can add guests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email classification uses unfiltered requested guests rather than guests actually added

Only `uniqueGuests` are persisted, but email sending receives the original `guests` array. For example, when a request contains one existing attendee and one new address, no row is created for the existing attendee, yet `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats that attendee as a newly added guest and sends them an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a booking confirmation) rather than the guests-added update. Pass the actual added addresses (`uniqueGuests`, after normalization) to the mailer.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest addresses are neither normalized nor deduplicated on the server

The API schema permits duplicate email addresses and this filter only excludes addresses already present on the booking; it does not deduplicate `guests` itself and compares addresses case-sensitively. A direct API caller can submit the same address repeatedly (or an existing/blacklisted address with different casing). Depending on the attendee database constraint this either creates duplicate attendees or makes the whole mutation fail, and casing can bypass the blacklist or create a second representation of the same mailbox. Normalize addresses and deduplicate them server-side before checking existing attendees, the blacklist, and `createMany`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

false_positives.candidate:
Attendee-initiated updates use the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's

The endpoint explicitly authorizes an existing attendee to add guests, but constructs `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. For an attendee request those credentials belong to the attendee, not the booking organizer whose destination calendar and event references need updating. The handler already loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Consequently attendee-added guests commonly fail to update the organizer calendar (or attempt an update with an unrelated account); construct the manager with the booking organizer's credentials for this operation.

Database attendees are committed before the calendar update succeeds

New attendee rows are written before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is called. If the calendar provider update fails, the mutation returns an error but the booking already contains the new guests; they receive no notifications and are absent from the external calendar. A retry may then reject them as existing, leaving the booking and calendar permanently out of sync. Handle/compensate for calendar failures or arrange the workflow so a failed external update does not leave silently committed attendee data.

The mutation permits adding attendees to cancelled or rejected bookings

After locating and authorizing the booking, the handler does not validate its status or whether it is still actionable. A caller can invoke this authenticated endpoint directly for a cancelled or rejected booking, creating attendee rows, updating the calendar, and emailing attendees that guests were added to an event that is no longer occurring. Reject non-active booking statuses (and define the intended past-event policy) before modifying attendees.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count updates can lose increments when cron invocations overlap

The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and writes `reminder.retryCount + 1` rather than using an atomic database increment. Two overlapping cron requests can both read 0, both fail scheduling, and both write 1; the reminder then survives another run despite two failed attempts. Overlapping invocations are also especially plausible while a reminder remains unscheduled. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update (and consider claiming the reminder/conditional updates to avoid concurrent scheduling) so the deletion threshold reflects actual failures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders

The new `retryCount > 1` branch is a top-level OR condition with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` restriction. Consequently, any EMAIL or WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` whose retryCount is greater than one will be permanently deleted by this SMS cron endpoint, even though this retry policy is intended only for SMS. Scope the retry-count predicate to SMS reminders (and, if appropriate, unscheduled reminders) so this job cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Reminders with no renderable message or recipient never consume retries

`retryCount` is only incremented after `scheduleSMS` returns false or throws. If `sendTo` is absent (possible because both the booking SMS number and workflow step recipient are optional) or message generation results in an empty value, this condition is skipped entirely. The reminder remains `scheduled: false` and is fetched on every cron run until its date passes, which leaves a common unsendable-SMS case unfixed by the retry cap. Treat an unusable recipient/message as a failed scheduling attempt, or delete/mark the reminder as unsendable.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Removing `findMany` breaks the exported service API

`findMany` was the service's data-access API and applied the authorization and filter predicates together with caller-provided `findMany` arguments. This change removes it and exposes only a raw SQL fragment, while no dependent call sites are migrated in this PR. Existing consumers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail to compile/run, and replacement callers must now independently choose the correct table/view and reimplement Prisma query features such as selection, ordering, pagination, and additional `where` clauses. Preserve a compatible query method or update all consumers as part of this change.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper cannot update env files on GNU/Linux sed

`sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, commonly used on Linux development environments and CI, the separate empty argument is not handled as the intended backup suffix and the command fails rather than updating `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Use a portable conditional for BSD versus GNU sed, or rewrite the file without relying on platform-specific `sed -i` behavior.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded US locale

The component uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")` even though its surrounding labels are localized through `useLocale`. Users with non-US locales will always receive US date ordering and formatting for the cache status, which conflicts with the localized UI. Format using the active application/user locale instead of a literal `en-US`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query

The delete-cache mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query supplying `cacheUpdatedAt`. When this component is used without a callback that explicitly refetches that query, a successful deletion leaves the UI showing the old cache timestamp and the delete action until a manual reload. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on mutation settlement/success (and optionally integrations if needed).

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellation writes are fired without awaiting completion

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but are invoked from `forEach` and their promises are discarded. The cancellation handler can return successfully before the email reminder has been marked `cancelled` (or an unscheduled/SMS reminder has been deleted). In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those unawaited operations may be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active and allowing cancelled-booking notifications to send. Collect and await these promises before completing the handler.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Normal reschedules still create immediate SendGrid cancellation entries

The primary booking-reschedule flow passes `true` as `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to immediately POST `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder as cancelled for the cron job. These cancelled scheduled-send entries remain counted by SendGrid until their send date, which is the capacity limit this PR is intended to avoid; after 100 pending cancellations, later reschedules can again fail to cancel and send stale reminders. This path should use the deferred cancellation mechanism (and preserve the reminder row for the cron), rather than `immediateDelete`.

One failed cancellation prevents all later reminders from being cancelled

All SendGrid cancellations are performed inside one try block. If `client.request` fails for any reminder, execution exits the loop immediately and no later reminders are cancelled during that run. Since the initial cleanup deletes email reminder rows once their scheduled date has passed, reminders skipped near their send time can lose their cancellation marker without ever having been cancelled at SendGrid, allowing them to be delivered. Handle failures per reminder (and retain failed rows for retry) rather than aborting the entire batch.

The raw SendGrid client used for cancellation is never authenticated

This handler only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the newly added cancellation path uses the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance at line 57. `sgMail` configures its own client instance and does not configure this exported raw client. Consequently the POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be unauthorized/fail, the catch block will swallow the error, and the cancelled reminders will remain scheduled in SendGrid and still be delivered. Configure this client with `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` before making raw client requests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Vital reschedule cleanup is detached from the enclosing error handling

`forEach(async ...)` does not await its callbacks. Consequently the surrounding `try/catch` only covers scheduling the callbacks; an import failure or `deleteEvent` failure is not caught, and the reschedule flow continues to email/return before cleanup is complete. Since `getCalendar` now always introduces an await point, this is reliably asynchronous rather than merely an unawaited provider deletion. Collect and await the callback promises with `Promise.all`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule endpoint fires calendar/video cleanup in an unawaited async forEach

Changing this callback to `async` makes every calendar deletion wait for module loading, but `forEach` discards the resulting promises. The mutation sends the reschedule email and returns without waiting for calendar/video cleanup, and failures from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` become unhandled promise rejections rather than an endpoint error/logged failure. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` (with explicit per-operation error handling as appropriate).

false_positives.candidate:
WipeMyCal reschedule cleanup is detached from the enclosing error handling

The new async `forEach` callback is never awaited. Calendar loading and deletion can still be pending when this function sends email and returns, while errors from either operation bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and can become unhandled rejections. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or an awaited loop so cleanup completion and failures are handled by this flow.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fixed-host override validation accepts slots that extend outside the override

The override check only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it, or starts exactly at the override end, falls through and is treated as available. For example, with a fixed host override of 10:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, an 10:30 or 11:00 slot can be returned for a round-robin event even though the fixed host is unavailable for part or all of it. The check must require the entire slot to be within the override interval, including rejecting equality at the end boundary.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty date overrides are compared by object identity and do not block their start slot

`dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so this condition is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Empty/zero-length date overrides (used to represent no availability) therefore fall through; the slot beginning exactly at that instant is considered available because neither subsequent strict boundary check matches it. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) and reject the override date as unavailable.

false_positives.candidate:
Override selection ignores timezone-driven date changes

Overrides are selected by comparing the unadjusted UTC-encoded `override.start` date to the invitee day, but their times are subsequently shifted by the organizer/invitee offset. When that shift crosses midnight, the override is applied to a different invitee calendar day than the one used by this filter, so it is omitted entirely. For example, an early-morning Asia/Kolkata override can correspond to the prior calendar day for an America/New_York attendee; requesting that attendee day will return regular availability instead of the override. Filter based on the override interval after converting it to the invitee timezone (and account for intervals overlapping the day).

Working-hours validation rejects valid slots for split schedules

The code uses `workingHours.find` to find any working-hours interval that does not contain the slot, rather than confirming that at least one interval contains it. With a normal split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected as soon as the first interval is examined, even though it is valid in the second interval. This can hide otherwise bookable round-robin slots for fixed hosts. The validation should accept when any same-day interval fully contains the slot, and reject only when none do.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Existing integrations without webhook sender metadata cause a server error

The comparison indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but `build_integration` creates GitHub integrations without a `sender` field and all integrations created before this change also lack it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed (or was created through the no-record branch above), a later installation attempt reaches this code and raises KeyError instead of returning the intended installation failure response. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as an unverified request and return the error page (or migrate/populate the metadata) rather than indexing it directly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
New installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check

When no Integration row exists yet, this branch immediately advances to integration creation without checking the GitHub account that installed the app. This is a normal race because the browser redirect from GitHub can reach this pipeline before the installation webhook has created the Integration containing `metadata.sender`; `build_integration` only fetches installation details and does not establish the installing user. A user can start their own valid Sentry/OAuth pipeline and submit a newly created/known installation ID during that window, causing the installation to be linked to their Sentry organization even though their OAuth user is not the app installer. The identity check must be performed from trustworthy installation/user data before allowing this branch, or the flow must wait for/require the webhook record with a sender.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`queued` timestamp is shared by every AssignmentSource instance

`timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource created for the lifetime of a worker process receives the same `queued` timestamp rather than the time that assignment was queued. This makes the serialized context metadata inaccurate (and will break any age/order logic added around this carrier). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the registered handler with `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so processing any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` will raise `TypeError` instead of safely evaluating as the previous concrete no-op handler did. Keep this handler on the non-stateful base until it is implemented, or provide implementations for all required stateful hooks.

true_positives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stateful detector evaluation documentation advertises the old list contract

The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, but the method now returns a dictionary keyed by group key. This is the extension point subclasses implement; following the documented contract would cause `process_detectors` to fail when it calls `.values()` on the returned object. Update the docstring to describe the keyed dictionary and its duplicate-key behavior.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the removed mark_failed module exports

This refactor removes the previously importable `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `SimpleCheckIn` symbols from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, but does not provide compatibility re-exports or update any consumers outside these four files. Any existing worker, integration, or test importing one of those non-private symbols from the old module will now fail at import time. Re-export the moved symbols from the old module (or update every caller in the repository and any supported downstream integrations) before merging.
